styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a clean, readable kura, but it is flatter than the references. The roof is a slate-blue block with horizontal row lines and a lighter ridge strip. It has no per-tile scallops or per-tile highlights, and only about 4 lightness steps against the references' 5-6 on their tile roofs. The white plaster walls are mostly one flat tone with little speckle or grain, and the namako checker base and door dots are the only real texture. The measured facts agree. Near-flat coverage is 6% against 0% for both references. Raw colours total 37 against 185 and 66. Visible tones per tile are 10 against 12 and 10, so they are close and I do not rely on that alone. Dark edges are only 28% neutral, so the outline leans toward a dark material tone rather than pure black, but I rate it mixed because the roof and window edges look uniformly dark. Overall it reads as more of a sticker than the hand-shaded references, with large plain wall and roof areas, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
